candidates.title: Another strong week for industrial rail freight
candidates.excerpt: U.S. weekly rail traffic totaled 537,397 carloads and intermodal units, up 4.85 compared with the same week a year ago, the Association of American Railroads (AAR) said. Traffic for the week ending September 26 totaled 235,787 carloads, up 3% compared with the same week in 2025, while intermodal volume of 301,610 containers and trailers was 6.3% higher compared to the same week in 2025. Seven of the 10 specific carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They were led by metallic ores and metals, 9.5%; petroleum and related products, 9.4%; and chemicals, 7.2%. Shipments of farm products excluding grain and food fell by 3.3%, followed by coal, 2.1%, and motor vehicles and parts, 1.8%. Coal inventories are up 1.4 million tons since the end of 2025, while domestic consumption was down 11.4% y/y. candidates.title: U.S. weekly rail volume again above 2025 levels
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — Continued intermodal strength again assured that weekly U.S. rail traffic remained above 2025 levels. The Association of American Railroads reports that traffic for the week ending Sept. 26, 2026, was 537,397 carloads and intermodal units, a gain of 4.8% compared to the same week a year ago. The overall figure included 235,787 carloads, up 3%, and 301,610 containers and trailers, up 6.3%. For the year to date, total volume is 19,458,578 carloads and intermodal units, an increase of 3.5% over the first 38 weeks of 2025. The 8,679,882 carloads represent a 2.7% increase while the 10,778,696 intermodal units are an increase of 4.1%. North American volume for the week, as reported by nine U.S., Canadian, and Mexican railroads, was 733,610 carloads and intermodal units, up 3.5% over the corresponding week a year ago. candidates.title: Behind the America 250 locomotives
candidates.excerpt: Behind the America 250 locomotives SPENCER, N.C. — The flanks of a diesel locomotive are not generally regarded as an artist’s canvas. And one would think a color palette with a primary focus of red, white, and blue could not yield spectacular and stunning results. Guess again! For the 250th anniversary of America’s independence, 68 railroads, businesses, railroad museums, and tourist lines painted more than 113 units with patriotic designs [see “An America 250 livery recap,” June 5, 2026]. Considering all the juts, angles, and curves of a locomotive and the limited color selection, the graphic results were impressive. From Aug. 28-30, 31 of these patriotic locomotives, along with five red, white, and blue TTX boxcars, and a Bicentennial Erie Lackawanna bay window caboose, gathered at the North Carolina Transportation Museum for the America 250 Locomotive Celebration. candidates.title: BNSF completes capacity projects in Illinois, Arizona, Tennessee
candidates.excerpt: FORT WORTH, Texas — BNSF Railway has completed three major projects to expand network capacity, the company has reported. At Galesburg, Ill., a second lead track has been added at the hump yard, completing a project announced earlier this year [see “BNSF adding a second hump lead …,” Trains.com, March 30, 2026]. The project expands the yard’s capacity from approximately 2,000 to 2,300 cars per day. “The way the Galesburg yard was configured results in tracks on the east side of the yard being unable to directly reach the hump crest,” Craig Rasmussen, assistant vice president of engineering services & structures, said in a press release. “The second lead connects into these tracks, allowing operational flexibility with more tracks available to arriving inbound trains.” At Winslow, Ariz., track work has eliminated delays that resulted when trains had to change or service locomotives. candidates.title: Port of Bilbao strengthens reefer logistics links with new Americas services
candidates.excerpt: The Port of Bilbao is strengthening its position in temperature-controlled logistics, supported by two new direct container services connecting the Spanish port with markets across the Americas. The new connections include a service linking Bilbao with the west coast of South America, with calls in the Dominican Republic, Colombia, Panama, Peru and Chile, alongside another direct service with Canada. These routes complement Bilbao’s existing shipping network, which connects the port with around 900 ports worldwide and has a particularly strong presence in the United Kingdom, Ireland and northern Europe. Reefer infrastructure supports perishable cargo Bilbao has developed dedicated infrastructure for handling fruit, vegetables and other temperature-sensitive cargo. Its container terminal, the largest in northern Spain, provides 540 reefer container sockets. Automated access is also available to streamline terminal operations and cargo movements. candidates.title: Maersk revises Fremantle equipment positioning charges
candidates.excerpt: Maersk will revise its import and export Equipment Positioning Service charges for all container types moving through Fremantle, Australia. The new tariffs will apply from 1 October 2026 for non-regulated countries and 23 October 2026 for regulated countries. Both charges will increase by AUD 24 per container, equivalent to approximately 11.4%. Maersk said the revisions support the continued provision of its service portfolio and network reliability.

candidates.title: Savannah’s Ocean Terminal renovation passes 60% completion
candidates.excerpt: Renovations at the Port of Savannah’s Ocean Terminal are now more than 60% complete. Georgia Ports Authority (GPA) is investing US$1.6 billion in the project. Once completed, the upgraded terminal will have an annual container capacity of 1.75 million TEUs. This compares with 200,000 TEUs before the redevelopment. Meanwhile, GPA has completed the terminal’s 2,650-foot berth. The upgraded berth is now ready to handle larger vessels. “Ocean Terminal is a major part of our strategy to prepare Savannah for future growth. The renovated berth is fully completed and ready for big ships,” said Griff Lynch, CEO, Georgia Ports Authority. For now, GPA will continue to handle smaller vessels at Ocean Terminal. The first phase of the renovated container yard is expected to be ready by mid-autumn 2027. The entire yard project is scheduled for completion by the end of 2028. candidates.title: Australian private credit manager Metrics gates funds
candidates.excerpt: Australian private credit manager Metrics gates funds Australian alternative credit manager Metrics Credit Partners has suspended investor withdrawals from some of its funds in the latest sign of stress in the country’s A$200bn (£106bn) private credit market. The firm, which manages around A$40bn, has temporarily suspended applications and redemptions in the unlisted wholesale funds behind its listed trusts after disclosing earlier this week that its auditor, KPMG, had disagreed with how some of their assets were valued, according to ASX filings. KPMG has also said it will not be able to sign off the listed trusts’ financial reports by the 30 September deadline. The freeze follows Metrics’ decision on Monday to suspend trading in three of its ASX-listed funds: two private credit funds, Metrics Master Income Trust and Metrics Income Opportunities Trust, and its real estate debt and equity fund, Metrics Real Estate Multi-Strategy Fund. candidates.excerpt: Union Pacific has deployed its first two battery-electric locomotives in Southern California, beginning a field-testing program intended to assess the technology’s reliability and operational fit in freight service. The two Wabtec FLXdrive locomotives are the first half of a four-unit order by Union Pacific (NYSE:UNP). The railroad said the remaining two battery-electric units are scheduled to arrive in October, completing a fleet that will operate in the greater Los Angeles area. The railroad said the tests will yield data on the units’ performance, reliability and operating capabilities. The 20-year-old, 2,490 teu MSC Hermes III was reported to have sent a distress call at around 08:45 hrs SGT on 22 September and was rebroadcast by Singapore MRCC according to the Maritime & Port Authority of Singapore (MPA). The 25 crew of the vessel were reported to have abandoned ship into a lifeboat and were rescued by another MSC vessel MSC Ruby which answered the distress call. Two other MSC vessels MSC Florentina and the MSC Turin III also diverted to the vicinity of the MSC Hermes III that appeared to be adrift around 300 km east of Vietnam. The naming ceremony was attended by RCL’s senior leadership, Dr. Jamlong Atikul, Chairman of the Board of Directors, Sumate Tanthuwanit, Chairman of the Executive Committee of RCL, and Dr. Twinchok Tanthuwanit, President of RCL, along with industry guests and stakeholders. The three newbuilds are the first in a series of eight container ships being built by RCL at CSSC Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding. candidates.excerpt: A BNSF train carrying mixed freight caught fire during a burglary in Riverside, California, Thursday morning. The train was traveling from Los Angeles to Chicago, BNSF told FreightWaves. Firefighters found an open upper container burning on the moving double-stack train. Officials have not identified the items inside or reported any stolen cargo. Riverside dispatchers received the first report at 4:40 a.m. near Chicago Avenue. Early information placed the train heading west from downtown. Crews later located it moving east between Spruce and Columbia streets. Riverside Fire Department deployed 19 firefighters, four engines, one truck and a chief officer. Crews move train for access Access problems prevented crews from reaching the flames at their first location. Incident commanders directed railroad personnel to reposition the equipment farther east. The organization said Peter Appel will take the helm as the next Chief Executive Officer, while Tim Kubiak will join AITX as the president and Chief Operating Officer and Eric Eng will take the position of Chief Strategy Officers. The organization said the new leadership would help it advance its strategy to “deliver more integrated railcar solutions that help freight shippers navigate increasingly dynamic supply chain logistics.” Appel will lead that strategy. Since November 2025, he has served as AITX’s interim CEO. Prior to that, Appel spent 12 years as Managing Director, Head of Rail at ITE Management, overseeing the company’s rail platform and growing it into one of the largest railcar fleets in North America and Europe. candidates.excerpt: Texmaco Rail Gets Two Orders Worth ₹131.36 Crores Texmaco Rail has bagged two domestic orders worth ₹131.36 crore for wagon manufacturing and supplies. While the smaller contract from TCI must be delivered within 16 weeks, the larger order from its joint venture partner Touax Texmaco is slated for completion by May 2027. Market snapshot: Texmaco Rail & Engineering Limited has secured two separate domestic orders collectively valued at ₹131.36 crore. The mandate comprises a ₹24.48 crore contract from Transport Corporation of India Limited and a ₹106.88 crore related-party contract from Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing Private Limited. Data Snapshot - Texmaco Rail secured two domestic orders totaling ₹131.36 crore. - The order from Touax Texmaco Railcar Leasing is valued at ₹106.88 crore for the supply of 4 BFNS rakes and 4 brake vans. - The contract from Transport Corporation of India is valued at ₹24.48 crore for the supply of 1 ACT wagon rake and 1 brake van.
